blocks.text: SriMukhwakSloka:

In this dark age of Kaliyuga symbolised by a pair of scissors, The rulers have turned themselves into butchers. Dharma or Moral values have disappeared from public life. The truth, symbolised by Moon, has been eclipsed in this darkest phase. Here I write the Legend of the First Mahal (Nanak) (How Nanak took Birth)
Dohra:

Then Captain Murry asked me once again, That I must narrate the whole story (of Guru Nanak). With all the details of the year and the age of his birth, Along with the name of the place and the country of his birth. (1)
lines: Then Captain Murry asked me once again,
That I must narrate the whole story (of Guru Nanak).
With all the details of the year and the age of his birth,
Along with the name of the place and the country of his birth.

blocks.text: Rattan Singh's version :
Chaupai:

The year of Guru Nanak's birth falls in the Bikrami Era2 , Guru Nanak was born in the year 1526 (1469 CE). His birth place was Rai Bhoi Bullar's village of Talwandi, Which is situated in the vicinity of Lahore towards Kasur (Pakistan). (2)
lines: The year of Guru Nanak's birth falls in the Bikrami Era2 ,
Guru Nanak was born in the year 1526 (1469 CE).
His birth place was Rai Bhoi Bullar's village of Talwandi,
Which is situated in the vicinity of Lahore towards Kasur (Pakistan).

blocks.text: It was in the caste of Bedis, a subcaste of Kashtriyas3 , That Guru Nanak took birth in this family of Bedis. It was a family of very religious and pious lineage, In which Guru Nanak took his human birth.(3)
lines: It was in the caste of Bedis, a subcaste of Kashtriyas3 ,
That Guru Nanak took birth in this family of Bedis.
It was a family of very religious and pious lineage,
In which Guru Nanak took his human birth.

blocks.text: It was under the constellation of auspicious stars in Satyuga4, That the Prophet Narsimanh had taken human birth. In the age (yuga) of Treta5 under a similar constellation of stars, Lord Rama had taken a human birth in that age. (4)
lines: It was under the constellation of auspicious stars in Satyuga4,
That the Prophet Narsimanh had taken human birth.
In the age (yuga) of Treta5 under a similar constellation of stars,
Lord Rama had taken a human birth in that age.

blocks.text: As Lord Krihna was born under a similar dispensation in Duapar 6 , So was Guru Nanak Born in Kaliyuga7 in the same order. Guru Nanak's father was known by the name of Kalu Das, And his mother was known by the name of Tripta.(5)
lines: As Lord Krihna was born under a similar dispensation in Duapar 6 ,
So was Guru Nanak Born in Kaliyuga7 in the same order.
Guru Nanak's father was known by the name of Kalu Das,
And his mother was known by the name of Tripta.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Guru Nanak's family was perfect in piety and moral virtues, Although it was not so rich and sound in affluence.
Partly because of his family's piety and partly of his own volition, Guru Nanak was born here on the auspicious night of the full moon. (6)
lines: Partly because of his family's piety and partly of his own volition,
Guru Nanak was born here on the auspicious night of the full moon.

blocks.text: It was the most auspicious moment and under the most auspicious Zodiac sign, The most ideal constellation of auspicious stars. The most auspicious Zodiac sign and the most auspicious planet, And the most auspicious constellation of mellifluous planets. (7)
lines: It was the most auspicious moment and under the most auspicious Zodiac sign,
The most ideal constellation of auspicious stars.
The most auspicious Zodiac sign and the most auspicious planet,
And the most auspicious constellation of mellifluous planets.

blocks.text: Guru Nanak's birth ushered an era of name and fame for his family, Their fame and reputation spread manifold and wide. It marked a manifold increase in family's fortunes and influence, And God blessed the family with wealth and landed property. (8)
lines: Guru Nanak's birth ushered an era of name and fame for his family,
Their fame and reputation spread manifold and wide.
It marked a manifold increase in family's fortunes and influence,
And God blessed the family with wealth and landed property.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

When the earth was dug to bury his mother's post-natal placenta, Gold coins were sighted underneath the dug up earth. Feeling highly delighted and excited by this good omen, Guru Nanak's parents summoned the most learned pundit8 of their area. (9)
lines: When the earth was dug to bury his mother's post-natal placenta,
Gold coins were sighted underneath the dug up earth.
Feeling highly delighted and excited by this good omen,
Guru Nanak's parents summoned the most learned pundit8 of their area.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Pundit cast a horoscope of Guru Nanak's Nativity, He felt extremely pleased with his tabulation. He cast a glance at the child's (Guru Nanak's) face spell bound, And a gentle smile ran all over his face. (10)
lines: The Pundit cast a horoscope of Guru Nanak's Nativity,
He felt extremely pleased with his tabulation.
He cast a glance at the child's (Guru Nanak's) face spell bound,
And a gentle smile ran all over his face.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Making a thorough interpretation of Guru Nanak's horoscope, The Pundit gave instructions to the parents of Guru Nanak. He predicted that a perfect prophet had taken birth (in their family), And that they must pay obeisance and show reverence to the child. (11)
lines: Making a thorough interpretation of Guru Nanak's horoscope,
The Pundit gave instructions to the parents of Guru Nanak.
He predicted that a perfect prophet had taken birth (in their family),
And that they must pay obeisance and show reverence to the child.

blocks.text: Since this new-born was a child without any blemish, His fame was likely to spread far and wide. He gave him a name beginning with the letter 'N' , And named him Nanak after the prophet Narsimanh. (12)
lines: Since this new-born was a child without any blemish,
His fame was likely to spread far and wide.
He gave him a name beginning with the letter 'N' ,
And named him Nanak after the prophet Narsimanh.

blocks.text: Whosoever came to have a glimpse of his face, Became fascinated with his charismatic appearance. Even after having repeated glimpses of his pious face, The onlooker was never satiated with his glimpse. (13)
lines: Whosoever came to have a glimpse of his face,
Became fascinated with his charismatic appearance.
Even after having repeated glimpses of his pious face,
The onlooker was never satiated with his glimpse.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Some predicted that he would be a Sidh9 , Others predicted that he would be a prophet. Still others made predictions about his being a King, With all the regalia of an enthroned sovereign. (14)
lines: Some predicted that he would be a Sidh9 ,
Others predicted that he would be a prophet.
Still others made predictions about his being a King,
With all the regalia of an enthroned sovereign.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The affluent wished to make an offering of their wealth to him, And the poor too wished to contribute money to his service. Some wished to test the effect of his blessings after making their offerings, Others made promises of offerings after the fulfilment of their wishes. (15)
lines: The affluent wished to make an offering of their wealth to him,
And the poor too wished to contribute money to his service.
Some wished to test the effect of his blessings after making their offerings,
Others made promises of offerings after the fulfilment of their wishes.

blocks.text: As Guru Nanak's fame and reputation spread in the Kaliyuga, More and more people flocked to have a glimpse of him. Whosoever visited him, shared his heart's desires with him, And listened to his discourses about the unknown and the future. (16)
lines: As Guru Nanak's fame and reputation spread in the Kaliyuga,
More and more people flocked to have a glimpse of him.
Whosoever visited him, shared his heart's desires with him,
And listened to his discourses about the unknown and the future.

blocks.text: The father Kalu Das, impressed by his son's personality, Thought of a business proposition for his illustrious son. Being obedient, Nanak never disobeyed his father's instructions, And went on any errand that his father sent him to. (17)
lines: The father Kalu Das, impressed by his son's personality,
Thought of a business proposition for his illustrious son.
Being obedient,
Nanak never disobeyed his father's instructions,
And went on any errand that his father sent him to.

blocks.text: He kept on meditating on the sacred Name of God, And began his conversations with the invocation of God's Name. He rendered the same advice to his fellow playmates, And made them recite the name of the True God. (18)
lines: He kept on meditating on the sacred Name of God,
And began his conversations with the invocation of God's Name.
He rendered the same advice to his fellow playmates,
And made them recite the name of the True God.

blocks.text: Dohra:

He improvised a musical string instrument out of a dry reed, And handed it over to his companion Mardana10 . He sang the sacred hymns to the accompaniment of music, And all his playmates joined to sing in a chorus. (19)
lines: He improvised a musical string instrument out of a dry reed,
And handed it over to his companion Mardana10 .
He sang the sacred hymns to the accompaniment of music,
And all his playmates joined to sing in a chorus.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

If I narrate all the details of his childhood, Even a big volume would fall short to record his deeds. So restricting myself to the essentially core incidents, I wish to synopsize a few anecdotes from his childhood. (20)
lines: If I narrate all the details of his childhood,
Even a big volume would fall short to record his deeds.
So restricting myself to the essentially core incidents,
I wish to synopsize a few anecdotes from his childhood.

blocks.text: How he once engaged his fellowmates in a game, And how he restored a grazed crop to its original luxurious state. How Balwand11 once saw Baba Nanak's face with his own eyes, Being shaded with the spread out hood of a snake. (21)
lines: How he once engaged his fellowmates in a game,
And how he restored a grazed crop to its original luxurious state.
How Balwand11 once saw Baba Nanak's face with his own eyes,
Being shaded with the spread out hood of a snake.

blocks.text: How did many other miracles come to light, A few he himself witnessed; others he heard from others. This is how he developed a great reverence for Nanak, And honoured him after inviting him to his palace. (22)
lines: How did many other miracles come to light,
A few he himself witnessed; others he heard from others.
This is how he developed a great reverence for Nanak,
And honoured him after inviting him to his palace.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thus, Balwand invited and honoured Guru Nanak, And himself sat at his feet like an obedient son. And allowed him access to play in every corner of his palace, Inside, outside as well as his private bed chambers. (23)
lines: Thus,
Balwand invited and honoured Guru Nanak,
And himself sat at his feet like an obedient son.
And allowed him access to play in every corner of his palace,
Inside, outside as well as his private bed chambers.

blocks.text: Sortha:

As iron turns into Gold with the touch of Paras12, Rai Balwand also gained in reputation with the touch of Nanak's feet. When Captain Murray heard Nanak's account from me, He also got promoted to the ministerial position at Delhi. (24)
lines: As iron turns into Gold with the touch of Paras12,
Rai Balwand also gained in reputation with the touch of Nanak's feet.
When Captain Murray heard Nanak's account from me,
He also got promoted to the ministerial position at Delhi.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
When Guru Nanak grew and gained more awareness, He was sent for getting education to a priest. How Guru Nanak taught his priestly teacher instead, I narrated that account to Captain Murray. (25)
lines: When Guru Nanak grew and gained more awareness,
He was sent for getting education to a priest.
How Guru Nanak taught his priestly teacher instead,
I narrated that account to Captain Murray.

blocks.text: How Guru Nanak accomplished many other miracles, Which I did not narrate so as to restrict the size of this epic. How after Guru Nanak's marriage was solemnized. He named his two sons who were born to him. (26)
lines: How Guru Nanak accomplished many other miracles,
Which I did not narrate so as to restrict the size of this epic.
How after Guru Nanak's marriage was solemnized.
He named his two sons who were born to him.

blocks.text: How his father Kalu Das wanted his son to do business, And Wished his son to earn a fortune for himself. How Guru Nanak refused to toe the family line, And how his disobedience irked his parents. (27)
lines: How his father Kalu Das wanted his son to do business,
And Wished his son to earn a fortune for himself.
How Guru Nanak refused to toe the family line,
And how his disobedience irked his parents.

blocks.text: How he paid no heed to the family's business line, And instead started reciting hymns with a Rabab. How he passed most of his time with companion Mardana, And took no interest in the business dealings. (28)
lines: How he paid no heed to the family's business line,
And instead started reciting hymns with a Rabab.
How he passed most of his time with companion Mardana,
And took no interest in the business dealings.

blocks.text: Guru Nanak at Modikhana13 and A Dip in River Waiyeen
Dohra:

Guru Nanak came to be known as a careless romatic, Following his total lack of interest in worldly affairs. Hearing this news, Guru Nanak's brother-in-law Jai Ram, A resident of Sultanpur, came to verify this news. (29)
lines: Guru Nanak came to be known as a careless romatic,
Following his total lack of interest in worldly affairs.
Hearing this news,
Guru Nanak's brother-in-law Jai Ram,
A resident of Sultanpur, came to verify this news.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He took away Guru Nanak to Daulat Khan, Who was the Mulk Umrao14 of the territory of Sultanpur. He introduced Guru Nanak to the Sultanpur's Nawab15 , And got him appointed as incharge of his warehouse. (30)
lines: He took away Guru Nanak to Daulat Khan,
Who was the Mulk Umrao14 of the territory of Sultanpur.
He introduced Guru Nanak to the Sultanpur's Nawab15 ,
And got him appointed as incharge of his warehouse.

blocks.text: All those who are interested in knowing a detailed account, They should consult some other ancient manuscripts. Those who wish to listen to various other episodes during this period, May go through the various other available biographical records. (31)
lines: All those who are interested in knowing a detailed account,
They should consult some other ancient manuscripts.
Those who wish to listen to various other episodes during this period,
May go through the various other available biographical records.

blocks.text: I have given only a very brief account of these incidents, Exactly as I had narrated these to Captain Murray.
Then Baba16 entered into a very contemplative mood, And became totally disinterested and detached from every affair. (32)
lines: Then Baba16 entered into a very contemplative mood,
And became totally disinterested and detached from every affair.

blocks.text: He used to go to a river for his daily morning ablutions, Where he was always accompanied by a servant. One day, he dived deep into the river, And did not come out for a very long time. (33)
lines: He used to go to a river for his daily morning ablutions,
Where he was always accompanied by a servant.
One day, he dived deep into the river,
And did not come out for a very long time.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The servant, losing all hopes of Guru Nanak's survival, Raised an alarm and a lot of hue and cry. Hearing these cries that Guru Nanak had drowned, Daulat Khan, Sultanpur's custodian, also came running. (34)
lines: The servant, losing all hopes of Guru Nanak's survival,
Raised an alarm and a lot of hue and cry.
Hearing these cries that Guru Nanak had drowned,
Daulat Khan,
Sultanpur's custodian, also came running.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He ordered the nets to be cast in the river to trap his body, But had Nanak been there, then alone could he be traced. When Some people surmised about his having crossed the river, A thorough search was carried out across the other end. (35)
lines: He ordered the nets to be cast in the river to trap his body,
But had Nanak been there, then alone could he be traced.
When Some people surmised about his having crossed the river,
A thorough search was carried out across the other end.

blocks.text: When the foot-tracers and astrologers failed to trace him, The people felt that the current must have carried him away. There was much grieving and mourning at Jai Ram's house, And Daulat Khan also felt dumbounded and suspicious. (36)
lines: When the foot-tracers and astrologers failed to trace him,
The people felt that the current must have carried him away.
There was much grieving and mourning at Jai Ram's house,
And Daulat Khan also felt dumbounded and suspicious.

blocks.text: While this suspense continued for one or two days, Guru Nanak emerged out of the river on the third day. With a rag wrapped round his waist and a towel on his shoulders, He stood still and silent like a scarecrow in a field. (37)
lines: While this suspense continued for one or two days,
Guru Nanak emerged out of the river on the third day.
With a rag wrapped round his waist and a towel on his shoulders,
He stood still and silent like a scarecrow in a field.

blocks.text: Hearing this news, people rushed to the spot, And started rallying round Guru Nanak. Jai Ram also reached instantly after hearing, And Daulat Khan also felt very astonished (38)
lines: Hearing this news, people rushed to the spot,
And started rallying round Guru Nanak.
Jai Ram also reached instantly after hearing,
And Daulat Khan also felt very astonished

blocks.text: Dohra:
Daulat Khan also arrived at the scene, He brought Guru Nanak back home. But Guru Nanak remained completely silent and detached, Despite Daulat Khan's pleadings and entreaties. (39)
lines: Daulat Khan also arrived at the scene,
He brought Guru Nanak back home.
But Guru Nanak remained completely silent and detached,
Despite Daulat Khan's pleadings and entreaties.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Daulat Khan summoned the services of Hakeems17 , For Nanak must be afflicted with some serious disease. When Baba Nanak explained the psychic cause (of his silence) to the Hakeem, Daulat Khan felt relieved of his tension and fears. (40)
lines: Daulat Khan summoned the services of Hakeems17 ,
For Nanak must be afflicted with some serious disease.
When Baba Nanak explained the psychic cause (of his silence) to the Hakeem,
Daulat Khan felt relieved of his tension and fears.

blocks.text: There were daily confrontations between Guru Nanak and Muslim Kazis18, Some even branding him a magician or a necromancer. But Daulat Khan did not agree with any of their opinions, As he came to repose his complete faith in Baba Nanak. (41)
lines: There were daily confrontations between Guru Nanak and Muslim Kazis18,
Some even branding him a magician or a necromancer.
But Daulat Khan did not agree with any of their opinions,
As he came to repose his complete faith in Baba Nanak.

blocks.text: He believed him to be a supreme prophet of his age, And his whole family became followers of Guru Nanak. Baba Nanak treated both the Hindus and the Muslims without any discrimination, Whosoever came to him became Guru Nanak's follower. (42)
lines: He believed him to be a supreme prophet of his age,
And his whole family became followers of Guru Nanak.
Baba Nanak treated both the Hindus and the Muslims without any discrimination,
Whosoever came to him became Guru Nanak's follower.

blocks.text: He gave a message of truth to both the communities, And restrained both from indulging in acts of oppression. As he became more and more famous and popular, People came to seek his blessings from far and wide. (43)
lines: He gave a message of truth to both the communities,
And restrained both from indulging in acts of oppression.
As he became more and more famous and popular,
People came to seek his blessings from far and wide.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Daulat Khan had two wives, having married twice, But both the wives had no issues. After paying obeisance to Guru Nanak, both of them were blessed, With two sons each, who grew to be as brave as lions. (44)
lines: Daulat Khan had two wives, having married twice,
But both the wives had no issues.
After paying obeisance to Guru Nanak, both of them were blessed,
With two sons each, who grew to be as brave as lions.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Their names were Gazi Khan, Gazi Mast Khan, The other two being Mir Khan and Zolakh Khan. The two mothers made a public declaration that they were, Blessed with a Couple of sons each, with the grace of Baba Nanak. (45)
lines: Their names were Gazi Khan,
Gazi Mast Khan,
The other two being Mir Khan and Zolakh Khan.
The two mothers made a public declaration that they were,
Blessed with a Couple of sons each, with the grace of Baba Nanak.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Baba Nanak was contemplating over the issue, How to remain detached from the world. Since the world had already come to know of his presence, So he thought of getting away from the world. (46)
lines: Baba Nanak was contemplating over the issue,
How to remain detached from the world.
Since the world had already come to know of his presence,
So he thought of getting away from the world.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

How can the sun remain eclipsed forever Even if the sky is overcast with myriads of dark clouds? So also Baba Nanak's presence came to be talked about, His fame spread far and wide in a very short time (47)
lines: How can the sun remain eclipsed forever Even if the sky is overcast with myriads of dark clouds?
So also Baba Nanak's presence came to be talked about,
His fame spread far and wide in a very short time

blocks.text: How can a person resist shifting towards fire, Who had been under a severe grip of cold? So also those people found relief in Baba Nanak's company, Who were severely affected with pain and sorrow? (48)
lines: How can a person resist shifting towards fire,
Who had been under a severe grip of cold?
So also those people found relief in Baba Nanak's company,
Who were severely affected with pain and sorrow?

blocks.text: All the Hindu and the Muslim Saints and Sidhas, Possessing various degrees of spiritual powers, Came to see Baba Nanak after hearing of his fame, All of them went back acknowledging his spiritual supremacy. (49)
lines: All the Hindu and the Muslim Saints and Sidhas,
Possessing various degrees of spiritual powers,
Came to see Baba Nanak after hearing of his fame,
All of them went back acknowledging his spiritual supremacy.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Baba Nanak blessed those with fame who sought fame, He blessed those with knowledge who sought knowledge. With whatever desire one sought his grace, Guru Nanak directed him towards its realization. (50)
lines: Baba Nanak blessed those with fame who sought fame,
He blessed those with knowledge who sought knowledge.
With whatever desire one sought his grace,
Guru Nanak directed him towards its realization.

blocks.text: Udasees19 and Held Discussions with Sidhas20 Being overtaken by a sense of detached aloofness, Baba Nanak thought of traveling to other lands. He asked Mardana to accompany him, Who followed Baba Nanak with his Rabab21 . (51)
lines: Udasees19 and Held Discussions with Sidhas20 Being overtaken by a sense of detached aloofness,
Baba Nanak thought of traveling to other lands.
He asked Mardana to accompany him,
Who followed Baba Nanak with his Rabab21 .

blocks.text: Whenever divine inspiration dawned upon Baba Nanak, He would recite hymns to the accompaniment of music. Sidhas, Saints, Pirs22 and their followers rallied round him, Delivering his message, he proceeded further on his travels. (52)
lines: Whenever divine inspiration dawned upon Baba Nanak,
He would recite hymns to the accompaniment of music.
Sidhas,
Saints,
Pirs22 and their followers rallied round him,
Delivering his message, he proceeded further on his travels.

blocks.text: To whatever country Baba Nanak paid a visit, He sermonized people to dwell on God's name. He eradicated the idol worship of all kinds, The worship of Pirs, Prophets, gods and goddesses. (53)
lines: To whatever country Baba Nanak paid a visit,
He sermonized people to dwell on God's name.
He eradicated the idol worship of all kinds,
The worship of Pirs,
Prophets, gods and goddesses.

blocks.text: He dispelled people's faith in all kinds of exorcism, Such as in various kinds of talismans, tantric rituals and occult powers, He also dispelled people's faith in all kinds of spirits, Such as various kinds of ghosts, spirits and Gugapir23 . (54)
lines: He dispelled people's faith in all kinds of exorcism,
Such as in various kinds of talismans, tantric rituals and occult powers,
He also dispelled people's faith in all kinds of spirits,
Such as various kinds of ghosts, spirits and Gugapir23 .

blocks.text: Dohra:

Whichever country Baba Nanak paid a visit to, Whether inhabited by the Hindus or the Muslims, He advised the Muslim's to shun others' belongings as they shunned Pork, And preached the Hindus to shun others' share as they shunned cow's meat. (55)
lines: Whichever country Baba Nanak paid a visit to,
Whether inhabited by the Hindus or the Muslims,
He advised the Muslim's to shun others' belongings as they shunned Pork,
And preached the Hindus to shun others' share as they shunned cow's meat.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Delivering a message of truth in this way, Baba Nanak made both the communities follow truth. He explained the true import of the Koran to the Muslims, And explained the real essence of the Vedas to the Hindus. (56)
lines: Delivering a message of truth in this way,
Baba Nanak made both the communities follow truth.
He explained the true import of the Koran to the Muslims,
And explained the real essence of the Vedas to the Hindus.

blocks.text: Once Baba Nanak paid a visit to the town of Achchal Batala, Where Sidhas were holding their annual congregation. He entered into a debate with the Sidhas, But, the Sidhas, despite their spiritual powers, paled in argument. (57)
lines: Once Baba Nanak paid a visit to the town of Achchal Batala,
Where Sidhas were holding their annual congregation.
He entered into a debate with the Sidhas,
But, the Sidhas, despite their spiritual powers, paled in argument.

blocks.text: The defeated Sidhas then complained maliciously, Against Guru Nanak to another Sidha known as Bal Gudai24 . Undertook
Chaupai:
That another Sidha (Guru Nanak) had appeared on the scene, Who had robbed them of all their powers. (58)
lines: That another Sidha (Guru Nanak) had appeared on the scene,
Who had robbed them of all their powers.

blocks.text: Hearing these Sidhas, he felt very arrogant about his superior status, And boasted of defeating Nanak in debate at his seat. Hearing this challenge, Guru Nanak travelled to his seat of power, And after defeating him in debate, proceeded further. (59)
lines: Hearing these Sidhas, he felt very arrogant about his superior status,
And boasted of defeating Nanak in debate at his seat.
Hearing this challenge,
Guru Nanak travelled to his seat of power,
And after defeating him in debate, proceeded further.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Guru Nanak then reached Pak Patan25 in the province of Multan, Where he conversed with a Pir, a heir to the Seat of Baba Farid26 . He also held spiritual discussions with other saints at UchhanLo27 And vanquished them all in spiritual discourses. (60)
lines: Guru Nanak then reached Pak Patan25 in the province of Multan,
Where he conversed with a Pir, a heir to the Seat of Baba Farid26 .
He also held spiritual discussions with other saints at UchhanLo27 And vanquished them all in spiritual discourses.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
There were countless number of other Sidhas, Guru Nanak reached wherever he heard of any Sidha. Exposing their fake and fraudulent spritual powers, He made all of them follow the path of truth. (61)
lines: There were countless number of other Sidhas,
Guru Nanak reached wherever he heard of any Sidha.
Exposing their fake and fraudulent spritual powers,
He made all of them follow the path of truth.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thus, Baba Nanak travelled all over the Punjab, And made people follow the true path of religious worship. And organised many religious and spiritual congregations, And exhorted the people to follow the teachings of their respective faiths. (62)
lines: Thus,
Baba Nanak travelled all over the Punjab,
And made people follow the true path of religious worship.
And organised many religious and spiritual congregations,
And exhorted the people to follow the teachings of their respective faiths.

blocks.text: It is difficult to narrate and record, The whole account of Guru Nanak's life. Whosoever wishes to proceed further in this pursuit, May consult the Puratan Janam Sakhis28. (63)
lines: It is difficult to narrate and record,
The whole account of Guru Nanak's life.
Whosoever wishes to proceed further in this pursuit,
May consult the Puratan Janam Sakhis28.
